anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly + Storage Space Capacity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly: Stale, incomplete, or low-quality statistics cause the optimizer to misestimate cardinalities and choose inefficient execution plans.
MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly: Dead rows and old row versions accumulate because background cleaners cannot keep pace, inflating table and index size and adding visibility-check work.
Storage Space Capacity Anomaly: Data, log, or temporary areas run short of free space, leading to allocation failures, auto-extend stalls, or write errors.

When all three root causes appear together, the system exhibits a blend of misestimated plans, rapidly growing on-disk structures, and mounting space-exhaustion warnings. Execution plans may swing from index probes to full scans against bloated tables, spilling large hash or sort operations into already constrained temp space. Vacuum/cleanup workers run continuously yet fall further behind, and their own I/O or temp needs trigger "no space left" errors that abort or defer maintenance. Catalog views show diverging row-count estimates from reality, while tablespaces, WAL/archive areas, and temp segments fill at an accelerating rate. Clients experience erratic response times, sudden query cancellations, and eventually write-path outages when log or data files cannot extend.

Causally, MVCC bloat is the first amplifier: as dead tuples pile up, both the physical footprint and the statistical distortion of the tables increase. The larger footprint hastens storage saturation, while the distorted statistics misguide the optimizer into scan-heavy or spill-prone plans that generate even more temp files and WAL, further consuming space. Once free space dwindles, ANALYZE jobs and autovacuum struggle to allocate the scratch or WAL space they need, so statistics grow even staler and bloat removal slows further. This positive feedback loop—stale stats → bad plans → more I/O and bloat → less free space → hindered cleanup/analysis—swiftly degrades performance and pushes the database toward a full-stop space exhaustion event.

entry.official_definition: The time limit for regular expression matching operations performed by the regular expression engine.
entry.trigger_condition: A regular expression match operation exceeds regexp_time_limit.
entry.workload_impact: The regular expression operation is constrained by the configured time limit.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
